title: Introduce cost sandbox seeder + quant calibrator (synthetic sampling + telemetry)
author: Aisha Patel
description: Motivation: Onboarding tenants and running safe cost-driven rollouts requires a reproducible synthetic workload generator that can seed the prefiller/batcher pipeline with representative traffic, and a quantization calibration step tied to end-to-end unit econ telemetry. This PR introduces a 'cost-sandbox-seeder' CLI + library and a companion 'quant-calibrator' service to automate candidate quant profile evaluation under synthetic traffic. Goals: 1) let SREs & ML engineers run deterministic batch/caching experiments without touching live tenant traffic; 2) attach unit-econ telemetry to quantization experiments (latency, tokens-per-second, model-score delta); 3) provide an opinionated default export format for profiles to feed Redwood Optimize/autotuner. Changeset includes: - cost-sandbox seeder CLI that synthesizes request mixes, varying prompt lengths, seq-lens, and cache hit ratios; supports JSONL workload recipes and SDK hooks. - lightweight simulator to run requests through the same prefill + batching stack (in-process harness) to measure batching shapes and KV-cache hit/miss curves. - quant-calibrator: a service that (a) accepts model artifact + baseline profile, (b) runs synthetic workloads produced by the seeder, (c) emits per-profile telemetry and a ranked .qprofile candidate list. - telemetry bridge that tags calibration runs with linear ticket, tenant-scope, and experiment id; emits unit_econ.{cost_per_token,latency_p50,quality_delta} metrics. - integration tests and a e2e smoke script that demonstrates generating a profile and importing into Optimize. Why not reuse existing samplers? Existing samplers require live traffic or manual recording; attempting to rely on those for calibration increased noise and slowed iterations. This PR makes experiments deterministic, repeatable, and faster to iterate while preserving production-like batch shapes. Checklist: - [x] design doc linked (Linear ENG-1298) - [x] seeder CLI + library implemented - [x] in-process prefill batch simulator - [x] quant-calibrator service and HTTP API - [x] telemetry integration and tags - [x] unit + integration tests - [x] docs: quickstart and sample recipes (docs/redwood/sandbox-seeder.md) Rollout plan: feature branch merged to main behind feature-flag 'econ.sandbox.enabled'. Default is off in hosted; Dedicated teams may enable in private deployments. Short-term: invite Platform SREs and Optimize team to run calibration w/ 3 tenant recipes. Medium-term: wire outputs into Optimize autotune pipeline and make a 'dry-run' import flow in Console.

changed_areas_summary: New CLI (cli/seeder) for generating JSONL workload recipes and running local runs
A sandbox library (packages/sandbox-seeder) that composes request mixes
An in-process simulator (simulator/*) that exercises prefill + batching logic to collect batch shape histograms
A quant-calibrator service (services/quant-calibrator) that runs candidate quant profiles against synthetic recipes and emits unit econ metrics
Telemetry bridge to tag experiments and export unit_econ.* metrics to our telemetry pipeline
notes: Security review: data used is synthetic only; no tenant PII. PR scoped so that calibrator service runs in a 'dry-run' evaluation namespace unless feature-flagged. Performance note: simulator runs are CPU-bound and intentionally limited in parallelism to avoid masking quant latency effects on GPUs. Documentation: quickstart in docs/redwood/sandbox-seeder.md with sample recipes and recommended tenant-weight presets.
release_notes: Added cost sandbox seeder CLI and quant calibrator service for deterministic synthetic calibration of quant profiles; emits unit_econ telemetry and can export selected profiles for Optimize import.
